title: Setup's engine count still divides by engines the desktop cannot launch
instrument: a case in src/modules/setup/engine-state.test.ts: probes [claude_code not_found, codex not_found, nebius found, muse_code found], claude_code chosen; assert the summary does not say 'of 4' (expected 'none of the 2 can be used yet')
body:
## Summary
Setup's engine sentence counts every row `GET /engines` returns, including nebius and muse_code, which the shell cannot start, so "none of the 4 can be used yet" names engines a person cannot choose.

## Description
`src/athena/harness/engines.py` ENGINES is now (claude_code, codex, nebius, muse_code) since 0af7ed7b, and `probe_all` reports every one of them through `/engines`. The shell launches only `KNOWN_ENGINES` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/daemon.rs:90`, two ids). This round fixed the numerator (`usable()` in `apps/desktop/src/lib/engines.ts` now keeps only ENGINE_IDS, 40267a84), but the denominator `probes.length` at `apps/desktop/src/modules/setup/engine-state.ts:82-91` still counts all four. Fixed: the count and the "told of no engines" branch read only probes whose id is an ENGINE_ID (filter once where the probes enter, `stores/engines.ts` or `engine-state.ts`).

## Flow
- Person has Claude Code chosen and missing, no Codex, a Nebius key set or Muse installed
- Setup -> engineStateOf -> "none of the 4 can be used yet" (or before 40267a84, "1 of 4 ready, but another is chosen")
- Fix: filter probes to ENGINE_IDS where Setup receives them; extend engine-state.test.ts with the case

## Expected impact
A person on Setup reads a count of engines they can actually pick. Nothing else reads the denominator; risk is a fixture that relied on four rows.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - Setup's "N of M" counts only engines this desktop can start
Before: 4 rows counted, 2 launchable (walked against engines.py ENGINES and daemon.rs KNOWN_ENGINES)
After: 2 counted (predicted)
Method: simulation - the site is modules/setup, outside this round's write set, so no gate was run there
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/modules/setup/engine-state.ts:82 `const found = usable(probes).length;`
apps/desktop/src/modules/setup/engine-state.ts:86 `${found} of ${probes.length} ready, but another is chosen`
apps/desktop/src/modules/setup/engine-state.ts:91 `none of the ${probes.length} can be used yet`
src/athena/harness/engines.py:72 `ENGINES = (CLAUDE.name, CODEX.name, NEBIUS, MUSE.name)`
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/daemon.rs:90 `const KNOWN_ENGINES: [&str; 2] = ["claude_code", "codex"];`

title: Up to five long-lived /events streams share one host's six-connection pool
instrument: an e2e probe against the real daemon: mount Main on Mind (devices + sleep) and Surface (tasks) and her window (run + tasks), count concurrent GET /events connections at the daemon, then time a GET /health issued while a /run stream is open; A = today, B = one shared bus follower per window
body:
## Summary
Four stores each open their own `GET /events` stream through `followBus` (`apps/desktop/src/lib/fleet.ts:224`), so the two windows can hold up to five long-lived connections to the one loopback daemon, against Chromium's six-per-host HTTP/1.1 pool that WebView2 windows of one app share.

## Description
`followBus` is called by `apps/desktop/src/stores/devices.ts:72`, `stores/sleep.ts:106`, `stores/tasks.ts:73` and `stores/run.ts:2339`; each opens a fresh `/events` fetch and holds it until the daemon's 15 s quiet close, then reconnects a second later. Main mounts devices and sleep on Mind and tasks on Surface; her window runs run's follower and `companion/tasks.tsx`'s. Every `/run` turn stream and every relayed turn (`DaemonApi.turn`) is another long-lived connection to the same host:port. Past six, Chromium queues the next request, so a json call (a card's resolve, `/engines`) can stall behind streams that are only nudges. The realtime-events technique's shape is one subscription per client fanned out locally. Fixed: one bus follower per window (a module-level subscriber set in `lib/fleet.ts`), with each store registering a handler and a reconnect callback.

## Flow
- Main on Mind, tasks under the bell, her window open mid-turn
- 2-3 /events streams in Main, 2 in her window, 1 /run stream
- a resolve() POST queues behind the pool limit until a stream ends
- Fix: shared follower per window, stores subscribe to it

## Expected impact
Cards and json reads never wait behind notification streams; the daemon serves one /events stream per window instead of up to four. Risk: a store that relied on its own reconnect callback timing.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - at most one /events stream per window
Before: 4 followBus call sites, up to 5 concurrent /events streams across both windows (counted from the call sites and the scenes that mount them)
After: 2 (one per window), predicted
Method: simulation - counting live connections needs the real WebView2 windows and daemon; no in-tree instrument counts them yet
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/stores/devices.ts:72 followBus(() => LIVE.api(), devicesHandler(onChange), onConnected)
apps/desktop/src/stores/sleep.ts:106 followBus(
apps/desktop/src/stores/tasks.ts:73 followBus(
apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:2339 ? followBus(
apps/desktop/src/lib/fleet.ts:236 controller = new AbortController(); (one stream per follower)

title: Five copies of the daemon HTTP door disagree on what a failed fetch is
instrument: a test per client that feeds a fetch which rejects with TypeError('Failed to fetch') and one that answers 200 with a non-JSON body, asserting the caller gets ApiError(0, 'offline') / a named refusal; count of private json() implementations 5 -> 1
body:
## Summary
`DaemonApi.json` (`apps/desktop/src/lib/api.ts:582`) lets a refused connection escape as a bare `TypeError` and a non-JSON 200 as a `SyntaxError`, while four sibling clients that hand-copy the same door map the first to `ApiError(0, "offline")`.

## Description
The same request door is written five times: `lib/api.ts:582` (`DaemonApi.json`), `lib/chores-client.ts:457`, `lib/adopt-client.ts`, `lib/intake-client.ts` and `lib/spaces.ts` (each with its own `offline` helper at lines 76, 171, 40, 158). The four copies catch the fetch throw and read the body defensively; DaemonApi does neither, so nine stores that build `new DaemonApi(found)` (connectors, devices, engines, run, sleep, task-runner, tasks, voice, companion/live) receive "Failed to fetch" where every chores/adopt surface receives the "offline" reason it has copy for. Fixed: one exported door in `lib/api.ts` (token header, offline mapping, refusal parsing) that the four clients call.

## Flow
- daemon restarts between the endpoint read and the fetch
- a DaemonApi call rejects TypeError("Failed to fetch"); a ChoresApi call rejects ApiError reason "offline"
- surfaces that switch on `error.reason` show "unknown"/the raw message for one and plain words for the other
- Fix: extract `daemonJson(endpoint, fetch, method, path, body)` into api.ts; migrate the four clients

## Expected impact
One rule for "the daemon is not there" across every client; a reader of a refusal sees the same reason whichever store asked. Risk: a store that today matches on the TypeError message.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one daemon request door with one failure vocabulary
Before: 5 private json() implementations, 2 failure mappings (counted)
After: 1 implementation, 1 mapping (predicted)
Method: simulation - the migration touches four files outside this round's write set
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The console stage reads Calm once per render and misses an OS reduced-motion change
instrument: a Console test: motion setting 'system', fake matchMedia reduced=false, render; flip it to true and fire 'change'; assert Stage's calm prop is true without another state change (red today)
body:
## Summary
`apps/desktop/src/console/Console.tsx:129` passes `calm={resolveMotion(motion, systemPrefersReduced()) === "calm"}`, read at render, so turning on the OS's reduce-motion while the setting is "system" leaves the stage moving until something else re-renders Console.

## Description
`lib/motion.ts` says the resolved `data-motion` attribute is the only thing that should be read so "a person's choice and the OS's preference cannot disagree on screen" (`apps/desktop/src/lib/motion.ts:10-14`). `stores/settings.ts:322-326` does update `data-motion` on the media change, and `avatar/runtime.ts:250-255` re-reads on both a MutationObserver and the media query, but Console derives its own answer and subscribes to neither. Three renderings of "is she calm now": `isCalm()` (attribute), `calmNow()` (attribute else OS), Console (setting + OS at render). Fixed: a `useCalm()` hook in `lib/motion.ts` that subscribes to `data-motion` (MutationObserver) and Console reads it.

## Flow
- motion setting "system", stage animating
- person turns on Windows "Show animations" off (reduced motion)
- settings writes data-motion=calm; Console does not re-render; Stage keeps its calm=false
- Fix: lib/motion.ts useCalm hook (attribute-driven), Console uses it

## Expected impact
A person who asks the OS for less motion gets it at once on the depth stage, as everywhere else. Risk: an extra observer per Console mount.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the stage honours an OS reduced-motion change without a reload
Before: Console's calm prop changes only on a Console re-render (read from source; no subscription)
After: changes on the attribute write (predicted)
Method: simulation - the site is console/Console.tsx, outside this round's write set; the instrument is named
Result: better
Gate: none
